title: Finitely presented algebra over an intermediate algebra of finite type
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S'$ a commutative $R$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $\sigma:S'\to S$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Then $S$, viewed as an $S'$-algebra via $\sigma$, is of finite presentation over $S'$: there are integers $r,s\ge0$, polynomials $g_1,\dots,g_s\in S'[t_1,\dots,t_r]$ and a surjective homomorphism of $S'$-algebras $S'[t_1,\dots,t_r]\to S$ whose kernel is the ideal $(g_1,\dots,g_s)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00F4 (lemma-compose-finite-type, line 540), part (4), with its proof (lines 555-565)
